title: IELTS Listening Practice - Listening - Diet and Nutrition Trends
subject: Listening

questions.q:
### Context: Are we too fixated on protein? - 6 Minute English

**Watch the video (or listen to the audio context provided) and answer Questions 11-25.**

![Are we too fixated on protein?](https://img.youtube.com/vi/VsBSCbBm_NA/mqdefault.jpg)
[Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VsBSCbBm_NA)

**Questions 11–16**
Choose the correct letter, **a**, **b**, or **c**.

11. What does Georgie identify as her favorite source of protein?
questions.explain: Georgie states: 'I think I really like an egg. An egg is my favorite kind of protein.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 12. According to Neil, which of the following is now advertised as a 'high protein' product?
questions.explain: Neil lists advertised products: 'from shakes and yogurts to chocolate.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 13. Ruth Alexander mentions that pasta is now being produced using which ingredients?
questions.explain: Ruth Alexander says: 'Pasta made with lentils and chickpeas rather than wheat flour.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 14. According to Scott Dicker, how do consumers view protein compared to carbohydrates and fats?
options: They view it as equally unhealthy in large amounts.
They see it as having a continuous positive health reputation.
They are confused about its benefits.
questions.explain: Scott Dicker says: 'protein seems to have this continuous health halo on it... Consumers don't see any downside to eating protein.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 15. What is the definition of a 'health halo' in marketing?
options: A label given only to organic food.
A government ranking of nutritional value.
Perceiving a food as healthy based on a single feature.
questions.explain: Georgie defines it as: 'a marketing term which describes perceiving a food to be healthy based on a single feature... even if its overall nutritional value is poor.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 16. What does Dr. Karan Rajan say about the history of fiber consumption?
options: People have always eaten enough fiber.
Historically, people have not paid enough attention to it.
Fiber has always been more popular than protein.
questions.explain: When asked if we pay enough attention to fiber, Dr. Rajan responds: 'Historically probably not.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q:
**Questions 17–20**
Complete the sentences below. Write **NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS** and/or **A NUMBER** for each answer.

17. Global sales of protein products are estimated to be around ______ pounds.
questions.explain: Neil states: 'Sales of protein products make around 7 billion pounds globally.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 18. Some products like yogurt are simply ______ as 'high protein' to increase sales.
questions.explain: Neil explains: 'products which already contain protein, like yogurt, are repackaged as high protein.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 19. The trend of trying to maximize fiber intake is known as ______.
questions.explain: Dr. Rajan mentions: '...optimizing their fiber intake and fibermaxing.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 20. Dr. Karan suggests adding ______ to snacks as a 'hack' to increase fiber.
questions.explain: Dr. Rajan suggests: 'adding certain seeds or nuts to snacks.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q:
**Questions 21–25**
Match the person (**A–E**) to the statement below.

A. Patrick Callahan
B. Ruth Alexander
C. Scott Dicker
D. Dr. Karan Rajan
E. Georgie

21. Was revealed to be the winner of the 2024 Mr. Universe contest.
questions.explain: At the end of the video, it is confirmed that Patrick Callahan is the winner of the Mr. Universe body building contest.
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 22. Mentions that bread is being fortified with beans and pulses.
questions.explain: Ruth Alexander lists products: 'Bread fortified with beans and pulses.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 23. Works for a market research company called SPINS.
questions.explain: Neil introduces him: 'Here's Scott Dicker from SPINS, a market research company...'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 24. Believes that the public interest in fiber is increasing (the tide is turning).
questions.explain: Dr. Karan Rajan says: 'I think the tide is turning and there is more people interested in fiber.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 25. Concludes that a balanced diet containing all food groups is likely the healthiest option.
questions.explain: Georgie concludes: 'In fact, the healthiest diet is probably a balanced diet, one containing items from all the major food groups.'
questions.subject: Listening
